extracted.intended_audience: Florida agencies, regulated parties, administrative-law practitioners, and members of the public who participate in Florida rulemaking or challenge administrative rules
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory procedural requirements and substantive criteria in the Florida Administrative Procedure Act governing publication, notice, petitioning, hearing procedures, and challenges to proposed, adopted, emergency, and unadopted rules. Useful for anyone drafting notices, filing petitions, or litigating rule validity in Florida.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of agency executive contact and indexing information
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of the section of the code dealing with an agency that files copies of its rules with the department, the department shall publish the address and telephone number of the executive offices of each agency, the manner by which the agency indexes its rules, a listing of all rules of that agency excluded from publication in the code, and a statement as to where those rules may be inspected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement governs what the Department of State must publish for each agency: contact info, indexing method, list of excluded rules, and inspection location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and incorporation of agency forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms shall not be published in the Florida Administrative Code; but any form which an agency uses in its dealings with the public, along with any accompanying instructions, shall be filed with the committee before it is used. Any form or instruction which meets the definition of 'rule' provided in s. 120.52 shall be incorporated by reference into the appropriate rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference must specifically state the form is incorporated by reference and include the number, title, and effective date of the form and an explanation of how the form may be obtained. Forms incorporated after Dec. 31, 2007 that are referenced in a rule notice must clearly display number, title, effective date, and rule number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and hyperlink restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The department shall allow adopted rules and material incorporated by reference to be filed in electronic form as prescribed by department rule. When a rule is filed for adoption with incorporated material in electronic form, the department's publication of the Florida Administrative Code on its website must contain a hyperlink from the incorporating reference in the rule directly to that material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The department may not allow hyperlinks from rules in the Florida Administrative Code to any material other than that filed with and maintained by the department, but may allow hyperlinks to incorporated material maintained by the department from the adopting agency's website or other sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Florida Administrative Register (FAR) content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAR must contain specified categories of notices and materials, including: (1) all notices required by s. 120.54(2) and (3)(a) showing text of all rules proposed for consideration; (2) notices of public meetings/hearings/workshops with agenda availability statement; (3) notices of requests to amend/repeal or adopt uniform rules; (4) notices of petitions for declaratory statements or administrative determinations; (5) summaries of objections filed by the Administrative Procedures Committee; (6) a list of rules filed for adoption in the previous 7 days; (7) list of rules pending legislative ratification; and (8) any other material required or deemed useful by the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAR is the official continuous revision and publication; items enumerated must be published to ensure public notice of rulemaking and related agency actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed FAR publication optional contracting
rubrics_metrics.description: The department may contract with a publishing firm for a printed publication of the Florida Administrative Register and make copies available on an annual subscription basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows supplementing electronic publication with print subscriptions where the department deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department authority to prescribe style and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The department shall prescribe by rule the style and form required for rules, notices, and other materials submitted for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must comply with departmental style/form rules when filing materials for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging agencies for Register space
rubrics_metrics.description: The department shall charge each agency using the Florida Administrative Register a space rate to cover the costs related to the Florida Administrative Register and the Florida Administrative Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost-recovery mechanism for publication services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of permanent record of notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The department shall maintain a permanent record of all notices published in the Florida Administrative Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures archival accessibility and historical recordkeeping of published notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAR website search, archival, subscription, and commenting capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Florida Administrative Register website must allow users to search for notices by type, publication date, rule number, word, subject, and agency; search a database making available all notices published for at least 5 years; subscribe to automated e-mail notifications of selected notices (notifications must include a summary of content); view agency forms and other materials submitted in electronic form; and comment on proposed rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional requirements intended to facilitate public access, timely notice, and participation in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent publication permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of material required by paragraph (1)(b) on the Florida Administrative Register website does not preclude publication of such material on an agency's website or by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may publish notices in multiple venues in addition to FAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency obligation to provide rule copies with legal citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide copies of its rules upon request, with citations to the grant of rulemaking authority and the specific law implemented for each rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures recipients receive rules with statutory authority references for transparency and legal context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency e-mail notification service obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency that provides an e-mail notification service to inform licensees or other registered recipients of notices shall use that service to notify recipients of each notice required under s. 120.54(2) and (3) and provide Internet links to the appropriate Secretary of State or agency web pages containing the proposed or final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures registered stakeholders receive required notices and direct links to relevant materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory metadata on published proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any publication of a proposed rule promulgated by an agency shall include, along with the rule, the name of the person or persons originating such rule, the name of the agency head who approved the rule, and the date upon which the rule was approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides accountability and provenance for proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAR access must be free
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the Florida Administrative Register website and its contents, including the e-mail notification service, shall be free for the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes cost barriers to public participation in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records Management Trust Fund deposit and cap
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees and moneys collected by the Department of State under this chapter shall be deposited in the Records Management Trust Fund; the unencumbered balance for fees collected pursuant to this chapter may not exceed $300,000 at the beginning of each fiscal year, and any excess shall be transferred to the General Revenue Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal rule governing fee handling and limit on fund balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance with publication/filing rules not admissible in rule-validity challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to comply with this section may not be raised in a proceeding challenging the validity of a rule pursuant to s. 120.52(8)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits procedural objections in certain rule-validity challenges; careful attention needed to which noncompliance is precluded as a defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary removal procedure when status of rule is in doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Department of State doubts whether a rule published in the official FAC is still in full force and effect, it shall request a written statement from the head of the agency or the Governor; publish the request and a copy in the FAR; if no timely response within 90 days, the failure to respond constitutes acknowledgment the rule is no longer in effect and is subject to summary repeal; notice of summary repeal must provide a 21-day period to file objections (petition under s. 120.56); appropriate respondent naming rules apply; after expiration of objection period or final decision, the Department shall update the FAC and provide historical notes explaining how the rule ceased to have effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the statutorily required steps, timelines (90 days to respond; 21 days to object), publication, and naming conventions for summary repeal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing and petition content to challenge a rule's validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person substantially affected by a rule or a proposed rule may seek an administrative determination of the invalidity of the rule on the ground that the rule is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority. The petition must state the particular provisions alleged to be invalid and a statement of the facts or grounds for the alleged invalidity, and facts sufficient to show that the petitioner is substantially affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial-affectedness and specificity of alleged invalid provisions and supporting facts are required for petitions under s. 120.56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing, notice, assignment of ALJ, and expedited hearing timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition challenging a proposed or adopted rule must be filed by electronic means with the division which shall immediately forward copies to the agency, Department of State, and committee. Within 10 days after receiving the petition, the division director shall, if the petition complies with content requirements, assign an administrative law judge who shall conduct a hearing within 30 days thereafter, unless withdrawn or a continuance for good cause is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good cause examples include written notice an agency will modify/withdraw the proposed rule or committee consideration of an objection. Failure to follow rulemaking procedures is presumed material but agency can rebut the presumption by showing petitioner substantial interests and fairness not impaired.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ decision timing, de novo hearings, and burden/standard of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the hearing, the administrative law judge shall render a decision and state the reasons in writing. Hearings under s. 120.56 shall be de novo in nature and the standard of proof shall be the preponderance of the evidence. The ALJ's order shall be final agency action (in these proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner and agency are adverse parties; other substantially affected persons may intervene on terms not unduly delaying the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines and burdens for challenging proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition alleging the invalidity of a proposed rule must be filed within statutorily enumerated deadlines (e.g., within 21 days after publication of notice required by s. 120.54(3)(a); within 10 days after final public hearing; within 20 days after statement of estimated regulatory costs or related publication). The petitioner has the burden to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the petitioner would be substantially affected; the agency then has the burden to prove by a preponderance that the proposed rule is not an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority as to the objections raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who becomes substantially affected by a changed resulting proposed rule may challenge any provision of the resulting proposed rule even if not initially affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ authority to invalidate proposed rules and effect of invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative law judge may declare the proposed rule wholly or partly invalid. Unless the decision is reversed on appeal, the proposed rule or provision declared invalid shall not be adopted. After a petition is filed, the agency may still proceed with other rulemaking steps including factfinding hearings; if part of a proposed rule is declared invalid, the agency may withdraw the proposed rule in its entirety at its discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must give notice of the ALJ decision in the first available issue of the FAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging adopted rules in effect — timing and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition alleging invalidity of an existing rule may be filed at any time while the rule is in effect. The petitioner bears the burden to prove invalidity by a preponderance. The ALJ may declare all or part of a rule invalid; the rule or part declared invalid shall become void when the time for filing an appeal expires. The agency must give notice of the decision in the FAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No filing deadline constraint for adopted rules; consequence is voiding of the rule or part once appeal period passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging agency statements as unadopted rules — petition content, stays, and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person substantially affected by an agency statement that is an unadopted rule may seek an administrative determination that the statement violates s. 120.54(1)(a). The petition shall include the text of the statement or description and facts sufficient to show it constitutes an unadopted rule. Upon notification before final hearing that the agency published a notice of rulemaking, such notice automatically operates as a stay of proceedings pending adoption; the ALJ may vacate the stay for good cause. If the ALJ finds an unadopted rule violates s. 120.54(1)(a), the agency must immediately discontinue reliance on the unadopted rule or substantially similar statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed rules addressing the challenged unadopted rule are later determined to be invalid exercises of delegated authority, the agency must discontinue reliance until proper adoption; proceedings under this subsection may be consolidated with others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special expedited timetable for challenging emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges to the validity of an emergency rule are subject to expedited schedules: within 7 days after receiving the petition the division director shall assign an ALJ who shall conduct a hearing within 14 days (unless withdrawn), and the ALJ shall render a decision within 14 days after the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very compressed timelines apply to emergency-rule challenges to provide rapid review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory statement petitions and agency duty to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Any substantially affected person may seek a declaratory statement regarding an agency's opinion on applicability of a statute, rule, or order to the petitioner's particular circumstances. The petition shall state with particularity the petitioner's circumstances and specify the statutory provision, rule, or order. The agency shall give notice of the filing in the next FAR and must issue a declaratory statement or deny the petition within 90 days; disposition is final agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaratory statement petitions provide guidance to regulated persons and have a 90-day statutory response requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural framework when substantial interests are at stake
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of s. 120.569 apply in proceedings in which the substantial interests of a party are determined. If the proceeding involves a disputed issue of material fact, s. 120.57(1) applies; otherwise s. 120.57(2) applies. Parties shall be notified of any order and provided information about available administrative hearings or judicial review, applicable procedures, and time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines which procedural subsection governs and requires clear notice of rights and time limits to parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency referral timetables, ALJ expertise assignment, and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency requests an ALJ, it must so notify the division within 15 days after receipt of a petition; a request for a hearing shall be granted or denied within 15 days. The division shall assign an ALJ with due regard to required expertise. All parties are entitled to a hearing after reasonable notice of not less than 14 days (which may be waived). Notice must include time, place, nature of hearing and the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures prompt referral and appropriate ALJ selection; petitions must contain items required by uniform rules and may be dismissed for noncompliance (with at least one opportunity to amend where cureable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings signature certification and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: All pleadings, motions, or other papers filed must be signed by the party, attorney, or qualified representative. The signature constitutes a certificate that the signer has read the document and that, based on reasonable inquiry, it is not interposed for improper purposes (harass, unnecessary delay, frivolous). Violation permits sanctions, including payment of other parties' reasonable expenses and attorney's fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourages frivolous or abusive filings and authorizes sanctions for misuse of process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer powers and discovery authority (limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may swear witnesses, take testimony under oath, issue subpoenas, and effect discovery by any means available to the courts and in the manner provided in the Florida Rules of Civil Procedure, including imposing sanctions, except contempt. However, no presiding officer may issue subpoenas or discovery orders to members or employees of the Legislature when the testimony sought relates to legislative duties; such subpoenas must show the testimony sought does not relate to legislative duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officers have broad investigative powers but constitutional/separation-of-powers limits apply to legislative personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility standards and handling of hearsay or similar-fact evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly repetitious evidence shall be excluded, but evidence commonly relied upon by reasonably prudent persons shall be admissible whether or not admissible in a court trial. Hearsay may be used to supplement or explain other evidence but is insufficient alone unless admissible over objection in civil actions. Similar-fact evidence of other violations is admissible when relevant to prove a material fact (motive, intent, identity, etc.) but inadmissible solely to prove bad character or propensity. When the state intends to offer other-act evidence, it must furnish to the affected party at least 10 days before the proceeding a written statement describing the acts and evidence with particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad pragmatic admissibility standard, with specific notice requirements when the state offers other-act evidence and constraints on propensity evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence handling, originals vs copies, and official recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary evidence may be received as a copy or excerpt; upon request parties shall have opportunity to compare the copy with the original if available. When official recognition is requested, parties must be notified and given an opportunity to examine and contest the material. Parties shall be permitted to conduct cross-examination when testimony is taken or documents are made part of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects parties' rights to verify documentary evidence and to test evidence through cross-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena challenge, enforcement procedures, and cost awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person subject to a subpoena may, before compliance and on timely petition, ask the presiding officer to invalidate the subpoena on grounds it was not lawfully issued, is unreasonably broad, or seeks irrelevant material. A party may seek enforcement of a subpoena or discovery order by filing a petition for enforcement in circuit court; failure to comply with a court order may result in contempt. The court may award prevailing party costs and attorney's fees as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural protections and remedies regarding compulsory process and potential fee awards to prevailing parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness attendance payment rates and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any public employee subpoenaed to appear at an agency proceeding shall be entitled to per diem and travel expenses at the same rate as state employees under s. 112.061 if travel away from headquarters is required. All other witnesses appearing pursuant to a subpoena shall be paid such fees and mileage as provided in civil actions in circuit courts. For public employees, expenses shall be processed and paid as agency travel reimbursement; for non-public-employee witnesses, payment shall accompany the subpoena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies witness compensation mechanics for agency proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content requirements for final orders in proceedings affecting substantial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless waived or extended with consent of all parties, the final order must be in writing and include findings of fact (if any) and conclusions of law separately stated, and it must be rendered within 90 days: (1) after the hearing if conducted by the agency; (2) after a recommended order is submitted to the agency and mailed to all parties if hearing conducted by an ALJ; or (3) after the agency has received the written and oral material it authorized to be submitted if there has been no hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of fact that merely track statutory language must be accompanied by concise and explicit statement of underlying facts of record. If agency head issues immediate final order for public danger, that order must recite with particularity the facts underlying the finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial scheduling order requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of any party, the ALJ shall enter an initial scheduling order to facilitate just, speedy, and inexpensive determination; the order shall establish a discovery period, a deadline by which all discovery shall be completed, and the date by which parties shall identify expert witnesses and their opinions, and may require parties to meet and file a joint report by a date certain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to structure the timeline of proceedings and set discovery and expert disclosure deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation order and burdens in third-party challenges to permits/licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: For proceedings under chapter 373, 378, or 403 where a nonapplicant third party challenges issuance of a license/permit/conceptual approval: the order of presentation is for the permit applicant to present a prima facie case demonstrating entitlement to the permit (by entering the application and supporting materials and agency staff report), followed by the agency. After the applicant's prima facie case and any agency direct evidence, the petitioner challenging issuance has the burden of ultimate persuasion and the burden of going forward to prove opposition through competent and substantial evidence. Applicant and agency may present rebuttal evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates burdens and evidence presentation order in environmental/permit-type administrative proceedings; specifies that this paragraph applies to proceedings under s. 120.574 and certain chapters.
